newsitem.title: USA: Texas Gov seen not reviewing lottery director.
newsitem.headline: Texas Gov seen not reviewing lottery director.

text.p: A news report that Governor George W Bush would meet with Texas Lottery Commission Executive Director Nora Linares to review her job performance Thursday was false, a spokesman for the governor said.
Bush spokesman Ray Sullivan called the report "absolutely incorrect," and "totally out of left field." Sullivan had no idea how such a rumor may have started.

"In fact, I'm very curious about that because a lot of the radio stations here were running it here this morning and people on my staff came in and said 'huh?,'" Sullivan said, adding that he placed a call to the news organization, which was trying to reach its stringer. The news organization has since corrected the report.

"I don't think that the governor would ever give the lottery director, regardless of who the lottery director is, a review," Sullivan said, adding that while the governor appoints the lottery commissioners. "She is hired and/or fired by the Lottery Commission members, and this is kind of mind boggling."

The Lottery has been mired in controversy of late, amid allegations of conflicts of interest involving some lottery officials, including Linares, and GTECH Holdings Corp the lottery's biggest contractor.
Lottery Commission Communications Director Steve Levine said the report did not emanate from his office either.
"I've got no idea where it came from," he said.
Levine said the Commission held a meeting Thursday, which lasted about 30 seconds.

"Yesterday, the executive director filed suit against the commissioners, and I assume because of that, but I not exactly sure if that's all the reasons, the chair cancelled today's meeting," he said. "They took no action, and they have scheduled a meeting for January 7."

Levine said it was inappropriate for him to discuss the nature of Linares' suit. In addition, Joe Morin, one member of the three-member lottery commission has resigned, the communications director said.
"He says his resignation is effective immediately, he was not here for today's meeting," Levine said. "Legally he serves until his successor is appointed and sworn in."
